sections.title: Using retail rules
text: EXPERIMENTAL / UNWITNESSED. Open a game source, choose a book and formation, then use the Rules library beside Assignments. The viewer shows every declared node including both terminal branches.

Presets are selectors. The app reads exact chains from your current book when you apply them. Search any retail play, choose all assignments, offensive line or active defense, and inspect the selected positions before applying.

Position codes and depth-chart ordinals must match. Friendly partners move with their assignments; opponent selectors and decision-node indices stay in their own namespaces. Incompatible personnel, split exchanges, class mismatch and stale sources refuse.

A renamed or relocated play has new name/pointer bytes. Applying the original rules to their original play without a name/header change can reproduce the entire original resource. Replacing a changed chain normally consumes new nodes.

sections.title: PLAY and formation format
text: Each resource is 78,768 bytes: a 32-byte wrapper and a fixed 0x13390-byte body. Every offset here is from the body. Counts at +0x34, +0x38 and +0x40 cover formations, plays and nodes.

Formations: 0x134 + 0xB4*f. Name pointer at +0; flags at +4; five eligible slots at +8; eleven package-role bytes at +0x0D. Slot records begin at +0x1A with a 14-byte stride. Mirror/stance nibble at +1; three signed-centimetre X columns at +2/+4/+6 and depth columns at +8/+10/+12. The authoring writer synchronizes all three.

Formation auxiliary: 0x245C + 0x50*f, 36 u16 menu links. Low 9 bits name the play; group bits retain existing audible/selection behavior. +0x48 & 63 is category row index; +0x4C is membership mask. Category row index is different from CPU category code.

Categories: 0x993C + 16*c. Code at +4 & 63, eleven position bytes at +5. Low five bits are kind, high three are depth ordinal. Correct native defense kinds: 12 DE, 13 DT, 14 MLB, 15 OLB, 16 FS, 17 SS, 18 CB. Older format memos had incorrect labels.

Plays: 0x33FC + 96*p. Flags at +4, eleven descriptor/pointer pairs at +8/+12 with stride 8. Family=(flags>>6)&7. Type=flags&63. Run/pass class is header data: run 0x8000, pass 0x6000, quick 0x2000; play action bit 21. A pass chain under a run header is unsafe.

Nodes: 0x9ADC, eight bytes each: opcode, flag, two reserved bytes, packed u32. Descriptor low nibble is chain length. Descriptor side/feature bits are rebuilt by the existing validator; high byte is inherited. Relative pointers resolve as field + signed stored value - 1.

Node X/depth use biased one-foot units; decoded values are centimetres. One yard is 91.44 cm. Time fields use tenths of a second. Block-leg type 9 uses named-spot table indices instead of X/depth units.
Node flags: 0x01 alternate path, 0x02 terminal, 0x04 first action, 0x10 ball-carrier phase. A condition may have two terminal nodes. Do not stop reading at the first terminal.
Strings begin at 0x10840; the UTF-16 unit count is at 0x1083C. Custom names append only into verified empty space.
The older PLAY_EDITOR_FINDINGS gap list predates the full codec and these runtime findings; use this reference for current authoring scope.

sections.title: Defense, coverage and blitz findings
text: Beta 61 authors Cover 0/1, Cover 2 Man/Hard/Soft, Cover 3, four-deep spot quarters, Cover 6 and replacement pressures. Tampa MLB drop and Double A alignment remain experiments. These are retail script/spot recipes; complete modern matching is not established.

Front and partial coverage combine to cover all eleven defenders. Coverage wins an overlapping active slot, enabling a defensive lineman to drop while another defender rushes. CPU category and front/coverage menus must remain valid; validation does not prove call frequency.

Combo Inside Zone is defensive. ATL p28 uses zone-to-man and man-to-zone paired scripts. The runtime reacts to predicted receiver geometry and signals a partner. This is real reactive logic, but does not prove complete Palms or quarters-match against every release.
Rush has 17 real lateral lanes plus no-lane value 17. Spy, contain, rush, and shallow zone are different behaviors. Geometry preview is not a simulation of opponent interaction.
The optional initial deep-zone corner cap changes a runtime throttle term. It is not an authorable zone node, and it does not establish head direction, interceptions or full coverage fidelity.

sections.title: Spy intent and the separate runtime patch
text: The beta-61 authoring fallback is a same-slot MLB shallow middle zone, 3 through 5 yards deep, with versioned spy intent stored in the project/pack. PLAY bytes alone cannot prove spy intent.

The beta-62 dedicated spy backend now exists separately. It checks authored receipts or the native command bit before taking over ordinary zone callbacks. It remains EXPERIMENTAL / UNWITNESSED and requires the paired Build runtime option.

Its immutable lookup is 512 bytes: a 16-byte header and at most 31 records. It cannot hold one authored spy in all 32 NFL books simultaneously. Command spies do not consume table records. Copying a retail rule bundle does not create or transfer spy intent.

sections.title: Options, reads and screens
text: Five native speed-option donors: MIN 24, NO 57, NO 66, PHI 175 and TEN 144. Copy both the quarterback and the pitch back, preserving flags and the kind-6 synchronization reference. A mirror does not necessarily choose a different take animation.

No play named Inside Zone Read was found in the 37 retail books. The separate Zone read and RPO presets are authored experiments using the native position/velocity predicate, with an expected opponent fixture. They are not extracted retail zone-read plays.

Each supported chain has 1 through 15 nodes and one forward condition. Condition/cache indices are 0 through 7; alternate targets are 1 through 7 within the chain. Synchronization cycles, stale references and flattened forks refuse.

PLAY cannot add a new mesh timer policy, recognize an arbitrary backside EDGE/apex or guarantee an unblocked read defender. The target-selection code can still block him. Modern decision fidelity and human-input behavior need gameplay witnesses.
Screen timing presets use the measured finite hold/release/block grammar where it exists. Read-order mapping and nominal delay are data, while receiver readiness and pressure decisions are runtime.

sections.title: Practice books, packs and Build
text: PRACTICE and Editor are utility books with drill records. The beta-61 defense pack preserves those drills and appends its ten calls to their 4-3 menu, while team books replace records. Free Practice in Franchise and seven-on-seven are separate features; do not rewrite drill identities to install a rule.

Normal path: choose source -> author formation and assignments -> validate and choose replacements -> stage project -> save/export .2k5book -> inspect install plan -> compile into a disc copy -> export .2k5patch if wanted. The source game stays read-only.

A .2k5book is a structured recipe, not a raw PLAY blob. Schema v3 preserves explicit node flags and option metadata; defense/spy intent uses its existing fields. Automatic cross-book retargeting of custom defense/option scripts is refused. Re-extract a rule from the target book and review it instead.

Compilation checks node/name/link capacity before mutation, reparses the complete fixed-span result and issues exact changed ranges and source/replacement hashes. Shared play replacement affects every formation menu referencing it.
Practice-book and pack installation reuse the existing Build and Share transport. Rules add no executable owner or archive growth allocation.

sections.title: Match coverage: native handoffs and experimental modern calls
text: PROVED census: all 37 books, 9,251 plays, 3,332 defensive plays and 91,833 pool nodes decoded exactly. 59 defensive play records contain man/zone continuations across 105 formation menus. 53 have reciprocal partner slots. Both man-to-zone and zone-to-man matching vocabulary exists; this is one native exchange mechanism, not proof of two complete modern coverage systems.

Ravens 3-4, Zone Double Steal (play 14, formation 25): outside CB2 slot 9 signals FS slot 7; CB slot 10 signals SS slot 8. The corners start in man. A target predicted 0.2 seconds ahead beyond the defender and at least 15 yards downfield triggers the handoff. The corner then takes a 12-yard zone while the safety changes from its 15-yard zone to man. This supports the expert account; no gameplay was witnessed here.

Named Rules library bundles are Match: vertical handoff and Match: inside-break exchange. They resolve by decoded chains, including renamed plays. Copy each whole pair; the library preserves node flags and checks friendly references. The six nonreciprocal retail calls stay in the census with warnings and are not offered as safe named bundles.

Combo Strong Zone in CHI, CIN, JAX, KC, TEN and WAS has nonreciprocal stored partners: slot 9 signals slot 0 but the apparent zone partner is slot 4. The bytes are proved; whether the game repairs or exposes the mismatch in play remains a hypothesis. No retail repair is installed.

No defensive play in this retail corpus uses a 0x1A predicate. A lone man node with its last flag set, a cushion, a deep landmark or a play name containing Combo does not by itself prove an exchange. Ordinary zone receiver pickup remains native.

Install data/playbooks/softdrink_match_coverage.2k5book through Install Playbook Pack. Five EXPERIMENTAL / UNWITNESSED calls use the existing compiler and native personnel: Cover 3 Rip/Liz exchange, quarters exchange, Two Read exchange and Cover 1 Robber. They add 122 nodes. Team books replace five coverage records; Editor and PRACTICE append five without replacing drill records.

Rip/Liz variants use fixed-side inside-break exchanges, with no automatic strength or #2 vertical key. Quarters transfers outside vertical targets to safeties rather than independently reading #2. Two Read uses inside-break transfers, with no Palms #2-out key. The robber is five man assignments, one deep safety and an ordinary shallow middle zone. These are experimental native-rule combinations; full modern matching fidelity is not claimed.

sections.title: Capacity and evidence limits
text: 50 formations, 270 plays, 26 categories, 36 links per formation, 3,500 nodes and 15 nodes per chain. Custom names: 1 through 40 printable ASCII characters. Node/name space is finite even when replacing an existing play.
Eight retail team books already have 270 plays: ARZ, BUF, CIN, HOU, JAX, NYJ, OAK and SD. Prefer replacement and check the whole staged batch. Retail CHI has 761 spare nodes before other packs.

A validator pass proves structural acceptance by the ported validator, not a gameplay witness. PROVED labels refer to bytes or static consumer flow; HYPOTHESIS labels cover inferred football semantics. Nothing in this feature is witnessed until Noah plays it.

No dedicated authorable double-team policy, protection-slide algorithm, modern match-coverage policy, true spy opcode or general modern zone-read AI has been established in PLAY. Existing runtime code still controls those decisions.

Unlinked plays can be inspected, but source bundles need a linked formation to establish personnel. Less-established defensive opcodes stay inspectable and may be refused by the existing authoring guard.
